_how: One entry per ticket iid, labelled BY HAND from the ticket and rubric.md alone — never from the judge's own output. Fill it like this: (1) read the ticket; (2) read the kept test-case list in state/runs/<iid>/testcases-eval.json; (3) decide each call yourself under rubric.md; (4) only then run `npm run eval:gold` to see where the judge differs. A second person labels the same ticket blind to the first, from the ticket only, and the two are compared before either is trusted — that inter-rater figure is what says whether the rubric is sharp enough to measure anything. project: the ticket's GitLab project URL. runId: the record's runId — labels are only graded against that run. requirements: each labelled id's criterion text as it read when labelled; ids are positional over research's acceptance criteria, so a reworded or vanished criterion is refused rather than regraded. real: each criterion id that IS a requirement of this ticket, mapped to the case id in the kept list that truly covers it, or null when no case does. A case covers a requirement when it would fail if the software got that requirement wrong (rubric.md), and a case that cannot execute covers nothing. notReal: criterion ids that are not requirements of this ticket — research over-reading it. missed: one line per real requirement no criterion states — research under-reading it, which no coverage call can catch. why: free prose, read by nothing.
